newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan lawmaker indicted in investment swindle.
newsitem.headline: Japan lawmaker indicted in investment swindle.

text.p: A prominent Japanese lawmaker was indicted on Wednesday in connection with a billion-yen investment fraud scandal involving his family members and possibly top-level opposition politicians, a Tokyo District Prosecutors Office spokesman said.

Upper House member Tatsuo Tomobe, 68, is the latest of five people, including his wife Mikiko, 61, and their son Momoo, 29, to be indicted in the affair involving bankrupt mutual aid society Orange Kyosai Kumiai, the official said.
Tomobe"s wife headed and his son managed the Orange group which prosecutors allege collected billions of yen from investors, he said.
"Tomobe is suspected of playing a central role in the case," the prosecutors office official said.

The lawmaker along with his wife, son and two others are indicted on charges of conspiring to swindle nine people out of 189 million yen ($1.53 million) from June 1994 to October 1996, the official said.
Mikiko, Momoo, Noboru Masukawa, 63, executive director of the society, and Matsunosuke Ishizaki, 62, former president of an affiliated company, were indicted on fraud charges Monday, he said.

Tokyo prosecutors allege Orange Kyosai, which was set up in 1986, collected 9.2 billion yen ($74.7 million) from investors, promising high interest returns on investments in an "Orange Super Fund" without any intention of actually investing the money.
Local media reports said a significant amount of the fund was used to support Tomobe"s election campaigns.
The Upper House lawmaker quit the main opposition New Frontier Party last November when the scandal surfaced but has denied the allegations.

Prosecutors will attempt to ascertain whether the society"s money was given to prominent politicians in order to buy Tomobe"s way into the main opposition New Frontier Party"s list of proportional representation candidates for the 1995 upper house election, the official said.
Tokyo prosecutors plan to file an additional indictment against the lawmaker in March for 300 million yen ($2.43 million) in unaccounted-for Orange Kyosai funds, the official said.
The additional indictment will come after prosecutors trace the money, he said.
